summary: memory-retrieval-warm keeps both warm windows 12 h instead of 30 min: the recall WorkerTaskPool idleTimeoutMs 18e5 -> 432e5 and SQLITE_IDLE_HANDLE_TTL_MS 18e5 -> 432e5 (dist/sqlite-handle-lifecycle-dWd9h3ii.mjs, same public module in 2026.9.6 and 2026.10.9). The deployed 30 min patch is a pinned predecessor, upgraded and rolled back through its verified original.
reason: S24 settled bench 31/10 (Gateway up > 1 h, 5 turns 90 s apart): warm turns 3.7-5.1 s (median 3.85 s vs 5.15 s before core#492), catalog -> start 0.4-0.5 s. The first turn after more than 30 min still took 7.6 s: the agent database handle had been closed by the shared 30 min idle window, its reopen queued an integrity quick_check while the session write waited 2.6 s, and the recall worker respawned (catalog -> start 3.2 s). A spoken request after a long pause is the common voice case.

capabilities.reason: Two OpenClaw idle windows through the existing compatibility owner; no route, action or capability.

architecture.reason: Same pinned patch set and wiring as core#492; no new owner, store, scheduler or daemon. The recall pool keeps its memory-critical retirement; the daily integrity verifier is unchanged.

evidence: Gateway worker and SQLite handle lifetimes only; MCP tools and schemas unchanged.

limitations: The gain on the first turn after a long pause (~2.6 s queue + ~2.7 s respawn) is inferred from the timeline; it is confirmed only by a bench with a > 30 min pause after deployment.
Idle SQLite handles and the recall worker stay resident up to 12 h; settled RSS was 923 MB idle and 962 MB with both warm, re-measured after deployment.
The shared handle window also applies to the state read worker pool, the reclamation and transcript workers; their idle threads stay alive longer.
A Gateway restart (deploy, night) still starts cold.
rollback: companion-deploy.sh of the previous commit undoes the set when the previous manifest differs, then the previous runtime-sync re-applies its own; or --patch-set memory-retrieval-warm --rollback then a Gateway restart.
